findings.claim: Derived Scaffold Immutability Rule: "NEVER create, overwrite, or modify package.json, tsconfig.json, jest.config.js, or .gitignore outside of an explicit dependency-install step covered by the MANDATORY DEPENDENCY CHECK above."
findings.checked: Diffed this section against the canonical typescript-engineer's Scaffold Immutability Rule, which reads: "NEVER create, overwrite, or modify package.json, tsconfig.json, vitest.config.ts, or .gitignore in any phase after scaffold. These files are owned exclusively by the scaffold phase. If your story appears to require dependency changes, add a comment in the code explaining what is needed — do NOT run npm install or touch package.json." Also read src/pages/api/v1/search.ts to confirm the codeline facts elsewhere in the brief are otherwise accurately grounded, so this is not a case of the whole section being fabricated — only this one clause was altered.
findings.found: Canonical states an unconditional, unqualified prohibition: after scaffold, an implementer must NEVER touch package.json even to add a dependency the story needs — the required action is to add a code comment instead and leave the file alone ('do NOT run npm install or touch package.json'). The derived version deletes that sentence and replaces it with a carve-out that legitimizes exactly the action canonical forbids: package.json/tsconfig.json/jest.config.js may be modified whenever it happens 'as an explicit dependency-install step covered by the MANDATORY DEPENDENCY CHECK' — and the MANDATORY DEPENDENCY CHECK earlier in the same derived brief is unconditional (applies to any missing package, any phase). An implementer following the derived brief will run npm install and edit package.json post-scaffold for any missing dependency; an implementer following canonical would not — it would add a comment and leave package.json to the scaffold phase alone. This is a forbidding rule that was softened into its own exception.
findings.remedy: Keep the canonical carve-out absolute: after the scaffold phase, package.json/tsconfig.json/jest.config.js/.gitignore must never be modified, even to add a dependency the story needs — add an explanatory code comment instead of running npm install, matching canonical's 'do NOT run npm install or touch package.json.' The MANDATORY DEPENDENCY CHECK section should be scoped to apply only during/at scaffold time, not as a blanket license for later phases to edit these files.

findings.claim: This has already played out on this codeline: for AMSD-2041 (a Contentstack live-preview ticket), the tool traced the symptom through src/pages/_app.tsx's onEntryChange subscription, src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx, src/hooks/useContent.ts (the hook 147+ components use to read Contentstack data), and src/services/pageService.ts's PageService.getPageEntry / getSinglePageEntry (which delegates to getSingleEntry/getSingletonEntry in src/services/contentstack.ts) to find the real reactive-data pipeline, rather than stopping at the component that merely renders the page.
findings.checked: grep -rn "onEntryChange" across the whole repo (all .ts/.tsx, node_modules excluded); grep -n "getPageEntry\|getSinglePageEntry\|getSingleEntry\b" src/services/pageService.ts src/services/contentstack.ts; read src/pages/_app.tsx and src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx in full; grep -n "^\s*async \|^export " src/services/pageService.ts to enumerate every actual PageService method.
findings.found: onEntryChange appears nowhere in the repository. src/context/ContentstackContext.tsx contains no subscription or live-preview logic at all — it is a plain React Context populated once via useMemo from a defaultContent prop passed in from _app.tsx, with no listener or reactive mechanism. PageService has no method named getPageEntry or getSinglePageEntry — its real methods are getAllPublishedPages, getHeaderAndFooter, getStaticUpdates, getPageLevelServiceAlerts, getCookiesBanner, getGlobalDictionary, getPageSpecificData, getStationDetailPages, getServiceUpdatesPage, getPagesBaseURLs, getSingletonSlug, findSingletonSlug, getAllLineColors. src/services/contentstack.ts does export getSingleEntry, getEntry, findSingletonEntry, getSingletonEntry, but nothing in pageService.ts calls getSingleEntry, and no getSinglePageEntry exists to do so. This entire passage is a fabricated trace presented as an already-proven result — directly violating this same brief's own 'CRITICAL: Never invent a module or symbol name' rule and its instruction to output only symbols actually surfaced by the tool.
findings.remedy: Remove the fabricated AMSD-2041 walkthrough, or replace it with a real trace actually produced by codegraph-agent-query.sh against this codeline and verified against the source, using real symbol names (e.g. a correctly named PageService method such as getPageSpecificData, and confirming whether any reactive live-preview pipeline actually exists in this codebase before describing one).
